option_text:
OPTION 1: ECS Fargate with RDS Multi-AZ
RECOMMENDED for most use cases
Best for: Modern applications, teams wanting minimal server management, variable traffic
Cost: $350-700/month (depending on scale)

Key components and architecture:
- VPC: Three-tier design (Public/App/Data subnets) across 2 Availability Zones with /20 CIDR
- Presentation Tier: Application Load Balancer in public subnets
- Application Tier: ECS Fargate containers (0.5-1 vCPU, 1-2GB RAM) in private app subnets, auto-scaling 2-10 tasks
- Data Tier: RDS Multi-AZ (db.t3.small PostgreSQL/MySQL) in isolated data subnets with automated backups
- Networking: NAT Gateways in each AZ ($65/mo), S3/DynamoDB Gateway Endpoints (free), VPC Flow Logs to S3

SOC 2 compliance ready:
- Multi-AZ provides high availability (A1.1, A1.2)
- Encryption at rest with KMS for RDS and EFS
- Private subnets with security group isolation (CC6.6)
- IAM task roles with least privilege (CC6.1)
- Flow logs for network monitoring (CC7.2)
- Automated backups with 30-day retention

Cost breakdown:
- Fargate: $30-90/mo (2-6 tasks running constantly at 0.5vCPU/1GB)
- RDS Multi-AZ db.t3.small: $70/mo
- ALB: $23/mo + $0.008 per LCU
- NAT Gateways: $65/mo (2 AZs)
- Data transfer: $45/mo (500GB)
- VPC Flow Logs: $40-80/mo

Tradeoffs:
- Higher per-compute-hour cost than EC2 but you pay only for actual usage
- No server patching or OS management required
- Container experience helpful but not required
- Cold start can add 30-60 seconds for scale-up
